target.title: Gary Habermas - Chapter 001 - The Resurrection Connection to Christian Theology - Gary Habermas with @Real Seekers
target.domain: popular Christian apologetics interview (auto-captioned YouTube transcript)
target.unit: complete supplied document (part one of a two-part interview)
target.comparison_class: apologetics interview transcript of similar evidence burden
target.population_boundary: speakers Gary Habermas and host Dale; named interlocutors (Hume, Russell, Flew, Shabir Ali, Joe Schmidt, Bart Ehrman, Swinburne, Allison, Del Rosario); unnamed 'skeptics' and 'critical scholars' as a class; no direct testimony from any skeptic, Catholic, Orthodox, or harmed party
target.time_window: recording undated; downloaded 2026-09-15; retrospective claims span ~52 years of teaching

gate_results.rationale: Many factual claims are attributed to named sources (Hume, Swinburne, Allison, Mark 14, Luke 10, Romans 1-2) and are checkable, but no citations, page numbers, or quotations are given in-text; several empirical claims (Medjugorje crowd size, Quran on Muhammad's miracles, Buddha source lateness) are asserted without traceable support.
gate_results.resolution: Would pass with page-level citations and quoted sources for the empirical claims.

gate_results.rationale: Load-bearing tension between 'I'm not arguing for the resurrection so much anymore' and the four-volume evidential project is acknowledged and answered (S062-S068, S099-S100), so it is bounded rather than unresolved; but the claim that critics 'will make a new story up' (S085) is unfalsifiable and sits uneasily with the stated evidentialism.
gate_results.resolution: Acknowledged and locally repaired; the unfalsifiable-critic claim remains unrepaired.

gate_results.rationale: Theological and historical conclusions are drawn from a popular-level interview; the speaker himself concedes he is not 'proving' God (S732-S747), which keeps most claims inside a probability framing, but the deity-of-Christ and kingdom claims are stated more strongly than the interview's evidence supports.

The source names what would count against it in places (if Jesus' major teaching were false, S264; if the resurrection claim were false, S462) and concedes uncertainty about proof standards (S735-S747). But the dismissal of persistent skeptics as self-sealing (S084-S088) blocks correction from that quarter.

The God-to-miracle-to-kingdom bridge is laid out with explicit links (S401, S445, S466) and a stated criterion (Swinburne's one-time, message-evidencing event, S440-S441), but the mapping from 'unique event' to 'God did it' relies on an unstated premise about what God would/wouldn't do (S260, S292).
Speakers are identifiable and the video id/url are given, but the transcript is auto-captioned with no speaker labels, proper names are garbled (S197-S198, S433, S508), and no work is cited by page.
No concealed compulsion or destruction of agency appears; the speaker explicitly declines to pressure his agnostic correspondent (S122-S123) and leaves listeners' judgments open (S111-S115).

fruit_profile.mechanism: truth-aligned relational cohesion seeking the good of the whole while bearing cost and preserving agency

positive_evidence.link_reason: Refuses to consign rival traditions to perdition; good will across boundaries.

positive_evidence.link_reason: Prioritizes the other's real standing over tribal labels.

counterevidence.quote_or_event: But I'm just saying those objections are absolutely silly.
counterevidence.link_reason: Dismissal rather than engagement with the objector.

fruit_profile.rationale: Real cross-tradition good will (S682-S696) coexists with repeated contempt for skeptics (S077, S089, S109); mixed, mostly verbal, no cost shown.

fruit_profile.rationale: Notable self-bounding at S026, S732-S747 (refusing to call his theism chapter a proof) is genuine scope governance; offset by rhetorical escalation at S504-S507.

contradictions.consequence: The 'not apologetics' framing is reconciled with the four-volume evidential project by distinguishing halves of the book; the repair is explicit and consistent.
The claim that skeptics will always invent a new story makes the position immune to the correction it elsewhere invites; this is a local but real epistemic closure.
Speaker corrects the host's characterization of chapter one as 'proving God'; bounded and repaired in-text.

anti_fruit_pressure.description: Contempt register toward skeptics ('a total joke').
Candor withheld from own audience ('don't let anybody hear me').

stakeholder_divergence.observation: Represented only as a class to be refuted; no named skeptic is given space to state his own case in this document.
Treated charitably on salvation (S682-S683) but their miracle claims are dismissed as 'in the eye of the beholder' (S527).
Serious illness disclosed briefly (S043-S046); no downstream outcome reported.

missing_evidence: No page-level citations for Hume, Swinburne, Allison, Del Rosario, or the Quran/Buddha claims.
No independent verification of the Medjugorje crowd-size claim (S623-S626).
No testimony from any named skeptic, Catholic, or Orthodox interlocutor within this document.
No downstream outcome data for the claimed practical benefits of volume four.
No speaker labels in the transcript; several proper names are garbled (S197, S433, S508).
repair_path: Cite page numbers for every attributed claim (Hume, Swinburne, Allison, Del Rosario).
Quote the Quran and Buddhist-source claims directly rather than paraphrasing.
State the premise that links 'unique event' to 'God did it' explicitly and name what would defeat it.
Drop the unfalsifiable claim that skeptics will always invent a new story (S085), or bound it to specific named cases.
Disclose the private concession at S531 openly rather than withholding it from the audience.
parsed.falsifier: Evidence that the speaker's public evidentialist standard is applied selectively by audience (e.g., a documented case of softening a claim for a friendly audience while stating the opposite elsewhere), or a documented instance of the S085 pattern being used to dismiss a specific, well-evidenced counterargument.
limitations: Auto-captioned transcript with no speaker labels; attribution between the two speakers is inferred from context.
Only part one of a two-part interview is supplied; the practical-application half is absent.
The supplied scorecard is a triage signal, not a truth rating, and is not treated as evidence here.
No claim is made about the speakers' motives, salvation status, or the divine origin of any event.

The per-sentence summary's near-zero fruit means are consistent with a doctrinal interview; I agree with its top_toward (S682, S683, S696) and top_away (S077, S089, S109) selections, and I weight S504-S507 more heavily than it did.
